children: SentinelOne® (

), the AI Security leader, today unveiled the next chapter of its AI Security and autonomous defense strategy at OneCon 2026. The company introduced Singularity™ Agentic Detection and Response (ADR), available today in early access. It also unveiled Singularity ASOC (Autonomous Security Operations Center), an integrated suite powered by Purple Security Superintelligence that brings data ingestion and analytics, agentic investigations, and automated response for machine speed autonomous defense. SentinelOne also significantly expanded its PartnerOne program to arm partners to build and scale AI Security practices built on the Singularity Platform. Together, the announcements advance SentinelOne’s vision for the AI era: defend surfaces AI runs on and give defenders the advantage with AI.

In the span of a year, AI has moved from assistant to actor in the enterprise. Frontier models have advanced to levels unimaginable just months ago. Agents now hold real credentials, chain tool calls and act independently across the enterprise. Attackers are using the same frontier models to find and chain vulnerabilities faster than human teams can respond, upending tried-and-true security hygiene and best practices. High profile AI-driven breaches due to rogue and unintended agentic behavior are increasingly commonplace.
Defense has to run at machine speed, grounded in real telemetry, on the devices where AI work runs, with people still firmly in command. That is what SentinelOne is building.
AI Security: Introducing Singularity Agentic Detection and Response (ADR)

Singularity ADR discovers agents, enforces what they’re allowed to do, and detects and stops unintended and malicious activity in real time. It is a major step beyond the agent discovery and governance SentinelOne introduced in March. ADR pairs that governance with the behavioral prevention, detection and response SentinelOne runs on endpoints, cloud workloads and identities, and ties every agent action to its origin. Security teams see in one view what an agent was asked to do and what it actually did, and they can stop an agent mid-action without halting the workflow around it. ADR mitigates risks from both rogue internal agents and external attackers.

Singularity ASOC: From Alert to Action at Machine Speed

Security operations teams have already reached the limit of what human-paced work alone can cover. Alert volumes outrun staffing plans, detection engineering remains highly manual, and coverage thins on nights, weekends and surges, the moments adversaries choose to move.

Singularity ASOC answers with an integrated suite that runs connected data, agentic investigation and automated response as one continuous loop, with analysts directing the work. Purple powers the suite, delivering a system of models built to be faster and better than any human team at detecting, investigating and stopping attacks. Purple Agentic Investigation uses native and third-party security data to investigate alerts end to end, gather evidence and work toward a verdict.

Around it sit AI SIEM, Hyperautomation, and threat intelligence and IOC management, plus AI Data Pipelines with more than 50 out-of-the-box connectors to third-party sources, including other security vendors’ tools, so teams can investigate and respond across their entire security stack. Singularity Credits, with administrator-set guardrails, keep every automated action within the limits the customer defines.

Partners Build and Scale AI Security Practices

SentinelOne also expanded its PartnerOne program with new partner-led services for building AI security practices on SentinelOne’s Singularity Platform. Those include new Implementation Engineer certifications for SentinelOne Prompt Security, endpoint and identity protection, and AI SIEM, with a learning path that covers AI Data Pipelines and Hyperautomation.

Partners can join the Singularity ADR early access program today and use the new AI Recon Assessment Service to lead AI security conversations with prospects. Certified partners also receive delivery packages with scoping and sizing guides, statement of work templates and deployment runbooks. LevelBlue, GuidePoint Security and World Wide Technology are premier launch partners, with a broader rollout to the PartnerOne network in the coming months.
